name: CurlShot
tagline: Screenshot API with an MCP server for agents.
shortDescription: CurlShot turns a URL, HTML, or Markdown into a PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF, or scrolling MP4/WebM/GIF video through one HTTP request.
agentSummary: Agents can call the CurlShot HTTP API directly, read the OpenAPI 3.1 description and llms.txt, or connect to the hosted MCP server (take_screenshot, list_devices) to capture web pages as visual evidence.
bestFor: Website screenshots, full-page and device captures, HTML or Markdown to image/PDF, Open Graph cards, and agent workflows that need to see a rendered page.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: pages behind a login need cookies or headers; private and local addresses are refused; banner and ad blocking works on most sites but not all; some sites block automated browsers. Keep the access key secret and use signed links when embedding screenshot URLs in public pages.
pricingSummary: Public pricing page: free plan with 100 screenshots per month and no card; paid monthly plans from $19 for higher volume. Failed renders and cache hits are not counted.
authModel: Access key sent as the access_key query parameter, an X-Access-Key header, or an Authorization: Bearer header; an optional secret key signs links for public embedding.
accountCreation: Self-serve email signup creates an account and API keys in the dashboard; no card is needed for the free plan.
browserSupport: The home page online tool takes a screenshot from a pasted URL without an account; the dashboard handles keys, usage, and billing.

capabilities.detail: No dedicated CLI; every capture is a single cURL request, and the docs include cURL, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go, and Ruby examples.
GET or POST /api/v1/screenshot with a URL, HTML, or Markdown; documented options, async jobs with signed webhooks, and bulk calls of up to 100 screenshots.
Hosted streamable HTTP MCP server at https://curlshot.com/api/mcp with take_screenshot and list_devices tools.
The online tool on the home page captures a pasted URL in the browser without an account.
Self-serve email signup with no card for the free plan; keys are created in the dashboard.
Public pricing page lists plan quotas, rate limits, concurrency, and the rule that failed renders and cache hits are free; also available as Markdown.
Docs cover getting started, authentication, every option, errors, usage limits, webhooks, and bulk; each page has a Markdown twin plus llms.txt and an agent quick-reference page.
No dedicated test mode is documented; the free plan and the no-account online tool can be used to try requests before production.
